name: Making predictions that know their limits
gist: ML models should admit when they're uncertain. How do you quantify confidence, calibrate predictions, or provide guarantees that hold even on new data?
explain: A model trained on historical data makes a prediction on a new example. Should you trust it? Maybe the new example looks nothing like the training data, which means the model is guessing in unfamiliar territory. Maybe the prediction came from extrapolation far outside the region where the model saw examples, which usually leads to mistakes. Maybe the data has changed since you trained the model, so patterns that used to work no longer hold. A good prediction system should not only give an answer but also admit when it is uncertain. For critical applications like medical diagnosis or autonomous driving, a confident wrong answer is worse than an honest "I do not know" because a doctor can ask for a second opinion or a car can take the safe path.

The challenge is that neural networks are usually overconfident. They give a prediction and a score (called a confidence), but that score does not mean what it seems. A model trained on high-resolution images might give 95% confidence when shown a blurry image it has never encountered, even though it should be unsure because the image is outside its experience. Calibration is the process of making confidence scores match reality—if the model says 95%, it should be right about 95% of the time, not 70%, so users can make decisions based on the score. On top of calibration, you often want guarantees: promises about performance that hold even on data the model has not seen. These guarantees allow predictions to be used in high-stakes settings because someone taking the prediction can trust it will not fail silently.

Papers use several strategies. Some post-process predictions: take the model's output and adjust the confidence scores so they align with observed accuracy. Others add uncertainty layers directly into training: use Bayesian methods that maintain a distribution over possible model settings rather than a single point estimate, so uncertainty propagates through predictions. Conformal prediction is a recent method that provides mathematical guarantees without assuming anything about the data: it builds a set of predictions for each example and guarantees that the true answer is in that set more than 90% of the time (if you set the threshold to 90%). Some papers learn when to abstain: train the model to say "I do not know" on examples it cannot handle, so users know when to ask a human. A few use ensemble methods: combine many models and see if they agree, using disagreement as a signal of uncertainty. The theme is that predictions should come with an honest assessment of doubt.

papers.title: Adaptive Conformal Guidance for Learning under Uncertainty
papers.contribution: AdaConG improves performance and robustness under imperfect guidance; in gridworld navigation it accelerates convergence and achieves over 6× higher rewards than the best baseline.

papers.title: Inference of Online Newton Methods with Nesterov's Accelerated Sketching
papers.contribution: Achieves global almost-sure convergence with asymptotic normality guarantees and develops fully online covariance estimator with non-asymptotic convergence guarantees.

papers.title: Learning Permutation from Structure Without Supervision
papers.contribution: Improves training stability and final permutation quality across sorting and jigsaw reconstruction tasks and routing-style settings, particularly as problem size increases.

papers.title: Measuring Uncertainty Calibration
papers.contribution: The paper provides non-asymptotic, distribution-free methods with practical procedures for measuring calibration error on real-world datasets.

papers.title: What Does Thompson Sampling Optimize?
papers.contribution: Reveals Thompson Sampling's core insight through online optimization lens enabling principled understanding and improvement by comparing against Bellman-optimal benchmark.

papers.title: COMPASS: Robust Feature Conformal Prediction for Medical Segmentation Metrics
papers.contribution: Produces significantly tighter conformal prediction intervals than traditional baselines on four medical image segmentation tasks for area estimation of skin lesions and anatomical structures while maintaining valid marginal coverage.

papers.title: Calibrating Decision Robustness via Inverse Conformal Risk Control
papers.contribution: Provides finite-sample guarantees enabling practitioners to reliably evaluate and calibrate robustness according to cost-risk preferences.

papers.title: Colorful Pinball: Density-Weighted Quantile Regression for Conditional Guarantee of Conformal Prediction
papers.contribution: Provides exact non-asymptotic excess risk guarantees and demonstrates remarkable improvements in conditional coverage performance on diverse high-dimensional real-world datasets.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction for Early Stopping in Mixed Integer Optimization
papers.contribution: Reduces solve time by over 60% while guaranteeing 0.1%-optimal solutions with 95% probability on six problem families from the Distributional MIPLIB library.

papers.title: Conformalized Decision Risk Assessment
papers.contribution: CREDO delivers statistically rigorous yet practically interpretable risk certificates, strengthening alignment between algorithmic tools and human intuition.

papers.title: Depth over Fidelity in Fixed-Budget Noisy Evolution Strategies
papers.contribution: RB-PEM achieves consistent gains in high-misranking, budget-constrained settings across the COCO bbob-noisy suite and tasks including RL policy search and hyperparameter optimization.

papers.title: Distributional Consistency Loss: Beyond Pointwise Data Terms in Inverse Problems
papers.contribution: DC loss acts as a direct plug-in replacement for standard data consistency terms, avoiding overfitting to measurement noise without early stopping.

papers.title: Expectation Consistency Loss: Rethink Confidence Calibration under Covariate Shift
papers.contribution: Provides theoretically grounded mini-batch trainable scheme with sample complexity matching Expected Calibration Error on simulated and real-world covariate shift datasets.

papers.title: Non-Asymptotic Analysis of Efficiency in Conformalized Regression
papers.contribution: Bounds of order O(1/sqrt(n) + 1/(alpha^2*n) + 1/sqrt(m) + exp(-alpha^2*m)) reveal phase transitions in convergence rates across regimes.

papers.title: Prior-free Tabular Test-time Adaptation
papers.contribution: PFT3A enables prior-free tabular test-time adaptation addressing both label and feature shifts without requiring source domain or prior knowledge.

papers.title: Robust Sequential Experimental Design for A/B Testing
papers.contribution: Bounds the worst-case mean squared error of treatment effect estimates, validated on synthetic and real-world datasets from a technology company.

papers.title: Sample Margin-Aware Recalibration of Temperature Scaling
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art calibration across CNNs and ViTs on standard, long-tailed, and distribution-shifted benchmarks with minimal inference overhead.

papers.title: Singleton-Optimized Conformal Prediction
papers.contribution: SOCOP increases singleton frequency by over 20% compared to standard scores with minimal impact on average set size in image classification and LLM multiple-choice tasks.

papers.title: Trajectory-Aware Heuristic Learning for Combinatorial Search
papers.contribution: Consistently improve local ranking accuracy and downstream search performance on Rubik's Cube under matched computational budgets.
